messages:
alyssa: Observability alert: east1b GPU pool showing persistent packet loss on node-gpu-12..15, kernels timing out, ~20% request error rate. Investigating. :rotating_light:

mike: saw the same in dashboards, ingress retransmits spiking around 16:02 UTC. GPU memory churn and evictions on pod gpu-infer-*. Quick tail of node log:
```
2026-03-18T16:01:58Z network: tx_errors=124 rx_errors=130
nvml: ctx_switch_timeout on GPU0
```

devon: starting a soft drain of the pool to avoid hard evicts. Will set node label maintenance=true and reduce route weight in traffic-manager.

lia: +1. Can we shift traffic to east1a / west1b standby pools? What's capacity headroom?

jon: east1a has ~25% spare GPUs, west1b ~10% spare. I'll bump east1a weight +0.3 and west1b +0.1 in rolling increments.

mike: also switch autoscaler to aggressive-burst (scaleCoolDown=30s) for next 10m to give headroom.

ops-bot: command accepted: set-traffic-weight --route=gpu-infer --zone=east1a +0.3 --zone=west1b +0.1

devon: running drain steps now:
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-east1b -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl cordon {}
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-east1b -o name); do kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 ${n}; done
```

alyssa: note: preserve KV prefix cache for impacted tenants while we reschedule to avoid massive cold-cache churn. Lia can you toggle cache-preserve?

lia: on it — enabling prefix preservation for tenant groups A,B via cache-router; should cut rewarm token cost.

jon: first weight increment completed. Error rate dropped 20% -> 8% in ~90s, p95 latency improved slightly.

mike: still seeing io errors on node-gpu-14 and node-gpu-15, drain on those failed due to daemonset pods; opening provider maintenance ticket.

devon: marking the nodes as fenced so scheduler won't place new pods and forcing reschedule of remaining critical pods to backup pools.

alyssa: proposed plan: 1) continue soft-drain and fencing, 2) activate reserved-burst (Dedicated) for 15m to absorb traffic, 3) if IO not recovered by +30m, perform full evac and reprovision east1b. Agree? :thinking_face:

lia: agree. Finance FYI: expected incremental spend ~ $1.2k for burst window. cc @finance-team

infractl-bot: executing: infractl allocate-burst --pool dedicated-east1b --gpus 8 --duration 15m
infractl-bot: allocation accepted (id=brst-335).

mike: provider update: "ToR NIC flaps due to buffer exhaustion, partial hardware replacement scheduled in 45m." They asked us to keep traffic shifted until swap complete.

alyssa: OK monitor for 30m. If further degradation, we'll trigger full zonal evacuate and reprovision. Keep incremental updates and confirm when caches are stable. :eyes:

devon: action items recap: devon=soft-drain+fence, jon=traffic weight increments, lia=cache-preserve toggle, mike=provider ticket/updates, alyssa=coord / watch.

ops-bot: thread pinned to channel by alyssa

lia: quick note: enabling aggressive-burst has already added ~$1.4k of temporary compute; will reconcile in the cost runbook.

jon: current rolling stats after second increment: p99 latency 420ms -> 360ms, error rate 8% -> 3%. Trend looks positive.

alyssa: thanks team. Stand by for a +20m check-in or call if regression. If anyone sees error rate >10% re-open the thread immediately.
